I struggle to call this a mixed bag because the good is not nearly as present in quantity as the bad. The film is a bit too comfortable with it's source material I think. It most consistently preforms when it is working as closely to the stage show as possible, i.e. the famously good music is still good. However it does not manage to overcome any of the flaws of the original product, nor I think, particularly thrill in it's limited ability to translate stage to film. Choreography and set design are both at best, adequate which is a shame for a product which should shine in both areas. Costuming is a bit better, but is kept down by the Netflix gray smudge color grading. How can you produce a film in Oz and not have any color! A world of bright shades is reduced to smudgy pinks, dull greens, and little else that is not seemingly grey or earth tone. The film is far worse for not having put in the work to be as delightful to look at as the original Oz film. The story is not very good, there is basically no modification from the stage show to my understanding, and the show has always coasted by on the musical numbers over the story. The same structure remains here, made worse by the fact this is only part one and several more hours of story remain. Overall a pretty unremarkable thing, it managed to never make me consider stopping watching, but not much beyond that in terms of impact.

Pretty solid! This was certainly more up my alley than I expected it to be. Everything is very maximalist here, to the point of being visually overwhelming at times. There was clearly a great amount of care and detail put into the set design. The dialogue was fun and I was a big fan of all the words they came up with in here. It's a fun twist on The Wizard of Oz, which I'm ashamed to say I only generally know the story of. I also only just found out that Wicked is not, in fact, an original screenplay and was adapted from a play. Apparently I live under a rock. There are certainly some gripes I have here, with the biggest one being the music. Composition felt very flat and just unmoving to me despite all of its attempts at grandness. Mixing was horrible, you can't hear any of the instruments over the vocals half the time. Vocal performances are reminiscent of how I feel about TOOL and Angine de Poitrine; there's a high level of technicality and little to no feeling. Music can be a make or break thing in a MUSICAL, but this seems to be mostly genre-based personal taste whatever so I won't be too harsh. I also thought it looked very visually fake a lot of the time. My girlfriend pointed out that a lot of the sets were actually real, and a surprising amount of the movie was done practically, which I found difficult to believe cause, well... look!! It just looks CGI as all hell!! But apparently it's true, there was a lot of work on the set designs here, and maybe it's that they did TOO good of a job that my brain fills in that it must be fake. Even then, so many shots have this sort of saccharinity to them that feels very common in these high-budget blockbusters where everything is filmed in a green room. Speaking of green... I felt like they didn't know how to deal with the main character being green. I wanted them to either REALLY lean into her sticking out visually or actually coordinate the shots so that the colors all go together (bonus points for all the nature-y segments that are super green and she's sort of like camouflaged almost I thought that was kind of funny) but most of the movie seemed to be in this sort of awkward middle ground between the two. Maybe it's supposed to say something about her lived experience or whatever but I didn't get that from it either. It suffers from the same problem a lot of blockbusters with A-list actors do, which is that they spend all this money on the background and hardly have the characters interact with it! Maybe it's some shallow depth of field so we can't even see anything, or maybe there's a bunch of cuts so that they can split a complicated shot into more manageable chunks, or any number of other things, but it never feels like we're actually supposed to explore the frame!! Everything happens in the middle, everything is immediately apparent what it means and where you're supposed to look and the subtext always finds a way to rise to the level of text and yada yada yada yada boring pretentious stuff YES I KNOW ITS A CHILDRENS MOVIE YES I HAD THE SAME COMPLAINTS WITH STAR WARS YES THE PROBLEM IS PROBABLY ME but still!! Like I go on and on about, can we please just stop with the medium close up over the shoulder dialogue shots!? I guess through all the rambling what I'm really trying to say is that so much of the technical side of things is done right. It's got the budget, the sweeping sets, all the lighting equipment you could ever ask for, super high quality cameras, and yet... it feels like they just stopped there. You got the cameras, now USE them!! In all the grandiosity of the sets, it feels like there wasn't much thought put into visual language. I think this could have been a better movie if the budget was cut by 90%, because it would have forced people to think and get creative about how to film stuff! I think the whole writing a blank check is detrimental because creativity so often is fostered by limitation. But even after saying all that, it is undeniable that this movie is very fun to just sit back and watch. It's almost 3 hours but doesn't even feel like 2. Cynthia Erivo and Ariana Grande have wonderful chemistry, the writing here is very entertaining, and if I turn off the pretentious side of my brain, it's very easy to get swept away by all of the visual sugar here. I am even excited to see the second part!!

The cast is very good <3 : Ariana Grande, Jeff Goldblum, Michelle Yeoh, Peter Dinklage, Keala Settle, Idina Menzel <3 The acting feels off and the music and the dancing are mostly disappointing. The costumes and the make-up are not for me and the writing is very underwhelming. I like the special effects and the environment is beautiful :) The phasing and the editing are okay and the atmosphere is fine. All of the scenes fly by quite fast and the connections between the characters are decent. The setting is workable, but i don’t like the characters personalities. The emotions are something between good and bad, but the comedy is weak. The action scenes are not half bad at all and I must mention that the best part of the movie is the last scene of the movie where the song ”Defying Gravity” truly kicks in <3 As a whole and in the end Wicked (2024) is bad, even if it has a few good elements in it. It’s not enough to get out of the bad zone… So i can’t recommend it. And that’s all i have to say about Wicked (2024).

Okay, I am by no means a musical fan, I know blasphemy for a theater kid! Shoot me, but honestly I usually find them straight up just not interesting. So I'll start with the bad here and end with the good. The color grading is all over the place, some shots look phenomenal while others look incredibly bland or washed out. The pacing is also pretty rough, it's hard to care about the building of relationships when everything feels like it's happening within the same week, or even sometimes the same day. Like I don't give a fuck about the love triangle or Boq's lil romance suplot...most of the romance done in this is pretty wack. Finally the worst offender of it all...the fucking references towards the Wizard of Oz! Maybe it's not as egregious as I felt it was but like...it really feels like every little fucking thing needs to have a pointless explanation and cheeky little nod at the audience. The member berries are on crack and it made me roll my eyes every single time. Now the good, it's a fun watch, I was never bored. Maybe one scene had me slightly uninterested, but there's enough going on that it keeps your attention. The costumes and set design are really well done. Honestly, perfectly casted too, the characters are fun but the preformances are what stand out. For the most part the music is really good, Defying Gravity being the obvious stand out, I got straight chills in that scene. All in all, this is a fun but muddled concept, and obviously this isn't the films fault but the source material it is adapting. The conflicts are halfbaked and most of the time done in such a cartoonish manner you can't take anything seriously. While that is a huge blow to the entire plot...unfortunately the biggest blow is the relationship at the center of the film, the most important part, is just straight up not strong enough. I do not buy these two as friends. It feels like two people pretending to be friends or just keeping the peace because it's more work to be enemies. It's not tragic when the true goat of our story Elphaba loses her Glinda, cuz Glinda has always been a posh selfish person and one dance or the fact that she's not actively being an asshole is enough. There's no real growth or scenes of them being actual friends (besides a song of them at the Emerald City) to justify any of this crying. Maybe my mind will change when I get to the second part, but right now, it's a fine movie, an enjoyable time, but carries no real emotional weight for me.

Best moment: “Defying gravity”. That song and scene is the centerpiece of the musical and this (and the other) movie. It doesn’t disappoint. The song by itself already feels epic but the movie version puts a cherry on top. This small action interlude on the broom is a fun little break before it works toward that climax and note we have all been waiting for. Best quote: “I don’t cause commotions. I am one.” MVP: Cynthia Erivo. First, her voice is stunning. It is so crystal clear and she switches between emotional to powerful with the flip of vocal cord. Second, the acting matches the vocal performance. She gives Elphaba so much heart and a deep compassion but that fury beneath the surface is always brewing. It is an emotional performance in all areas. Best visual: The wizard’s room. The rest of the movie is so bright, colorful and joyful. That set, however, is darker and there isn’t any of the joy of the Emerald City. The design of the big head also looks really cool and ominous. Best showstopper: “Dancing through life” is just so much fun. The part in the library has so much cool choreography with the books and the spinning set. The ballroom looks stunning and also has some fun choreography. In all of this I ask myself one important question: How can someone be as charming as Jonathan Bailey? Rating: 9 out of 10 flying monkeys
